name: Planck's act of despair
scope: The reluctant birth of the quantum, told as a man cornered by data. T1: every hot thing glows a color set only by its temperature — a poker goes dull red, then orange, then white — and Wilhelm Wien's 1893 displacement law turns that into a thermometer you can point at a star (Betelgeuse red and cool, Rigel blue-white and hot, both in Orion tonight). T2: classical physics, applied honestly to a glowing cavity, predicted that opening an oven door should blast you with ever more energy at ever shorter wavelengths, without limit — the divergence Paul Ehrenfest only named the 'ultraviolet catastrophe' in 1911, a decade AFTER Planck. T3: Planck's fix — matter exchanges energy with light only in whole packets of size hv, so high-frequency modes cost too much to be excited at ordinary temperature and the curve bends back down; he fit h to Lummer and Pringsheim's cavity data and got about 6.55x10^-34 J s. T4 (corrected misconception): Planck was NOT chasing the ultraviolet catastrophe. What forced him was Heinrich Rubens and Ferdinand Kurlbaum's brand-new far-INFRARED measurements in October 1900, which showed Wien's law failing at LONG wavelengths; Rubens brought the numbers to Planck's house, and Planck had the interpolation formula that same evening. T5: Planck spent the next decade trying to derive his own result WITHOUT quanta, and failed; in a letter to Robert Williams Wood on 7 October 1931 he summed the whole thing up as 'an act of desperation.' Einstein, not Planck, was the first to take the packets seriously. Deeper rungs available: Kirchhoff's 1859 cavity-with-a-pinhole as the way to build a perfect emitter; Planck's Munich professor Philipp von Jolly telling him in 1874 that physics was essentially finished (Planck's own later recollection); the 1918 Nobel; and the modern vindication — COBE's 1990 measurement of the cosmic microwave background, the most perfect blackbody spectrum ever measured, whose error bars were smaller than the drawn curve.
source: Grokipedia 'Max Planck' (act of despair / 'lucky intuition', a decade of resistance, h fit to Lummer-Pringsheim data, von Jolly anecdote, 1918 Nobel) and Grokipedia 'Planck's law' (Kirchhoff 1859 cavity, Stefan 1879, Wien 1893 displacement, Rayleigh-Jeans divergence, 'ultraviolet catastrophe' named in retrospective analyses). Corroborated: wissenschaft.de 'Ein Akt der Verzweiflung' and en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Max_Planck for the 7 October 1931 letter to Robert Williams Wood ('Akt der Verzweiflung'); arXiv:1704.08309 and the researchgate paper "'..I didn't reflect much on what I was doing..' How Planck discovered his radiation formula" for the Rubens/Kurlbaum October 1900 far-infrared data as the actual trigger.
framing_note: DISCOVERY ladder, and the bank's best portrait of a discoverer who did not want his own discovery. THE ACCURACY RAIL: do not repeat the textbook fairy tale that Planck set out to solve the ultraviolet catastrophe — that name is Ehrenfest's from 1911 and the thing that actually cornered Planck was Rubens and Kurlbaum's long-wavelength infrared data; the T4 rung IS this correction, so no earlier rung may state the fairy tale as fact. Second rail: verify the Rubens house-visit date and the same-evening postcard before authoring T4; if only the October 1900 data can be confirmed, key the rung on the DATA, not the doorstep. Third rail: the von Jolly 'physics is finished' story is Planck's own late recollection in his Scientific Autobiography — tell it as his recollection. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: T1 (go outside, compare Betelgeuse and Rigel, read two stars' temperatures off their color) and T5 (the man who started quantum theory spent ten years trying to undo it). DISTRACTOR MINE: the real graveyard of blackbody theory — Wien's distribution law, the Rayleigh-Jeans law, caloric, the luminiferous ether, and Planck's own attempted classical rescues; plus real adjacent physicists (Wien, Rayleigh, Jeans, Lummer, Rubens, Boltzmann, Kirchhoff). Never joke options. INVERT THE WONDER: put the absurd prediction (infinite energy from an open oven door) in the stem and make the specific fix the answer.
history_overlap: HISTORY bank risk: Nazi-era German science and the 20 July 1944 plot (Planck's son Erwin was executed for peripheral involvement) — that episode belongs to history; this ladder must never spend a rung on it. PHILOSOPHY bank risk: Planck's principle ('a new scientific truth does not triumph by convincing its opponents... but because its opponents eventually die') is an epistemology claim philosophy may already carry as a seminar move — if used here at all, key it to Planck's own documented behaviour toward his own quantum, not to a general theory of scientific change.

name: Einstein's packets and the man who spent ten years trying to disprove them
scope: The photoelectric effect as a REVERSAL story with the best skeptic in physics as the co-star. T1: in 1887 Heinrich Hertz, busy proving Maxwell's radio waves were real, noticed his receiver's spark jumped more easily when ultraviolet light from the transmitter fell on the electrodes; he wrote it down and went back to the waves. T2 (the puzzle that broke wave theory): dim blue light knocks electrons out of a metal instantly, while red light of ANY brightness knocks out none at all — Philipp Lenard's careful 1902 vacuum-tube measurements showed brightness sets HOW MANY electrons come out and frequency sets HOW FAST, exactly backwards from what a wave should do. T3 (Einstein's 1905 answer, from the paper he himself called revolutionary): light arrives as countable packets of energy hv, one packet is absorbed by one electron, the metal charges a fixed toll (the work function) to let it out, and whatever is left over is the electron's kinetic energy. T4 (the measurement): Robert Millikan built an apparatus with a knife and a machine shop sealed inside the vacuum so he could shave a fresh, unoxidized sodium surface without letting in air, measured the stopping voltage against frequency for years, and got a straight line whose SLOPE is h/e — Planck's constant, measured all over again from a completely different phenomenon. T5 (the honest twist): Millikan had set out to DISPROVE Einstein. He published the confirmation anyway, and in the same 1916 paper still called the photon a 'bold, not to say reckless' hypothesis that 'flies in the face of thoroughly established facts of interference.' He accepted the equation and rejected the picture. T5b (what finally settled it): Arthur Compton's 1923 X-ray scattering, where a photon bounces off an electron like a billiard ball and comes away with a longer wavelength, plus Bothe and Geiger's 1925 coincidence experiment killing the last serious wave-only rival (the Bohr-Kramers-Slater theory). Einstein's 1921 Nobel citation names the photoelectric law — not relativity. Deeper rungs: Wilhelm Hallwachs's 1888 charged zinc plate discharging under UV (a demo a school can still run); Alexander Stoletov's 1888-1891 photocurrent law and first photocell; the modern descendants — solar cells, photomultipliers, the CCD in every phone camera.
source: Grokipedia 'Photoelectric effect' (Hertz 1887 spark gap, Lenard 1902 retarding-potential apparatus and the intensity-vs-frequency laws, Stoletov 1888-91 and the first photocell, Einstein 1905 'On a Heuristic Viewpoint', Millikan 1914-1916 verification and his value of h, the exact 1921 Nobel citation wording). Corroborated: National Academies Press biographical memoir chapter 'Bold, Not to Say Reckless'; Europhysics News, 'Millikan's struggle with theory' (2000); IOPSpark, '...and Millikan's manipulations'; Physics World, 'Einstein's revolutionary paper'; Acta Physica Polonica B 37 (2006), 'Einstein's revolutionary light-quantum hypothesis'.
framing_note: REVERSAL + MECHANISM ladder; the emotional spine is that the best test of a claim was run by a man who wanted it to fail and reported the result honestly anyway. THE ACCURACY RAIL: do not say Millikan 'proved Einstein right and was convinced' — the honest record is that he verified the EQUATION while still rejecting the PHOTON, and his 1950 autobiography softened his own history; T5 is exactly this distinction and must state it precisely. Second rail: Einstein's 1921 Nobel was for the photoelectric LAW, and the 1922 award ceremony/citation wording should be quoted, not paraphrased into 'he won for relativity, sort of.' DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: T2 (a blazing red lamp does nothing, a feeble blue one works instantly — brightness is not the same as punch) and T5 (a scientist publishing the result he was trying to destroy). DISTRACTOR MINE: real rival explanations serious people held — Lenard's 'trigger' hypothesis that light merely releases energy the electron already had, the luminiferous ether, classical wave 'energy accumulation' (which predicts a measurable time lag that was searched for and never found), and the Bohr-Kramers-Slater theory in which energy conservation was only statistical; plus real adjacent names (Hertz, Lenard, Hallwachs, Stoletov, Compton, Bothe, Geiger, Kramers, Slater). TEACH BEFORE TESTING: define work function and stopping voltage in an earlier rung before any rung depends on them. INTRA-SCIENCE LANE: this ladder owns the photon; the WAVE nature of light (Young, Fresnel, interference geometry) is the double-slit ladder's — key rungs here to the particle side only.
history_overlap: HISTORY bank risk: Einstein as a WWII figure (the 1939 letter to Roosevelt, the flight of physicists from Nazi Germany) — that is the history bank's episode; every rung here stays inside the 1905 paper and Millikan's laboratory. Also guard against duplicating any history-bank Nobel-Prize trivia: no rung may be a bare 'who won what in which year' question.

name: The double slit: one particle interfering with itself
scope: The flagship ladder — the experiment Feynman said contains the only mystery, and the one a kid can run on a wall tonight. T1 (the invitation): a five-dollar red laser pointer, a wall, and a single human hair held in the beam paints a row of bright and dark stripes — the same needle-shadow geometry G. I. Taylor used, and proof that light is doing something no stream of pellets can do. T2 (the original): in 1801 Thomas Young let sunlight through a pinhole, split the beam with a card about one-thirtieth of an inch wide, and read the wavelengths of the colors off the spacing of the fringes; his numbers are close to the modern values, and he reported it to the Royal Society in November 1801. T3 (one at a time): in 1909 G. I. Taylor dimmed a lamp with smoked-glass screens until, on average, roughly one photon at a time was inside the apparatus, then exposed a photographic plate for three months — the fringes came out just as sharp as with a bright source ('Interference fringes with feeble light', Proc. Camb. Phil. Soc. 15, 114). T4 (matter does it too): Claus Jonsson sent electrons through real slits in 1961; in 1989 Akira Tonomura's team at Hitachi filmed the pattern assembling itself dot by dot — 10 electrons look like random speckle, 140,000 electrons are unmistakable stripes. Physics World readers voted it the most beautiful experiment in physics. T5a (how big can it get): in 1999 Markus Arndt and Anton Zeilinger's Vienna group interfered C60 buckyballs — 60 carbon atoms, 720 amu, glowing hot at 900 K; in 2019 the same group ran molecules over 25,000 amu and up to 2,000 atoms through a two-metre interferometer, still getting fringes. T5b (the corrected misconception): put a detector on the slits and the fringes die — but NOT because the detector shoves the particle. Durr, Nonn and Rempe built an atom interferometer (Nature 395, 33, 1998) in which the momentum kick was measurably far too small to wash out the pattern, and the pattern died anyway. What kills interference is the CORRELATION that makes the path knowable. Deeper rungs: why two slits and not one (coherence); Davisson-Germer as the accidental first electron evidence (see the matter-wave ladder); the delayed-choice quantum eraser and what it does NOT show.
source: Grokipedia 'Double-slit experiment' (Young 1801 card ~1/30 inch and the Royal Society paper, Fresnel 1818, Davisson-Germer 1927, Jonsson 1961, Merli et al. 1974, Tonomura 1989, Feynman's 'only mystery'). Corroborated: G. I. Taylor, 'Interference Fringes with Feeble Light', Proc. Camb. Phil. Soc. 15, 114-115 (1909), via Springer 'The First Paper on Experimental Observation of Interference Fringes with Feeble Light' and the Skulls in the Stars post 'Taylor sees the (feeble) light (1909)'; Physics World, 'The double-slit experiment' (2002 most-beautiful poll) and IOPscience, 'The double-slit experiment with single electrons'; Arndt et al., Nature 401, 680 (1999) via Physics World 'Wave-particle duality seen in carbon-60 molecules' and Univ. Vienna QuantumNano 'The Origin: C60 Diffraction'; Fein et al., 'Quantum superposition of molecules beyond 25 kDa', Nature Physics 15, 1242 (2019); Durr, Nonn & Rempe, Nature 395, 33 (1998).
framing_note: THE flagship MYSTERY + test-it-yourself ladder of the whole sub-strand. T1 must be an INVITATION rung, not a fact rung: the answer is what the hair-in-the-laser-beam actually paints on the wall. Include the eye-safety line in the framing of the item so the parent can run it. THE ACCURACY RAIL: never let a rung say or imply that 'consciousness' or 'looking' collapses anything, and never let the delayed-choice quantum eraser rung suggest the future changes the past — the erased fringes only reappear when you sort the data by the idler outcome, and no signal travels backwards. Second rail: Feynman's line is 'a phenomenon which is impossible, absolutely impossible, to explain in any classical way, and which has in it the heart of quantum mechanics... In reality, it contains the only mystery' (Lectures Vol. III, ch. 1) — quote it exactly or paraphrase openly; no invented Feynman quotes anywhere in this ladder. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: T1 (do it on the wall) and T3 (three months of exposure, one photon at a time, and the stripes still show up). DISTRACTOR MINE: Newton's corpuscles, the luminiferous ether, 'the particles bump into each other on the way through', 'the detector's kick pushes the particle off course' (the specific idea Rempe's experiment ruled out), and the observer-consciousness picture that von Neumann and Wigner really did entertain; plus real adjacent names (Young, Fresnel, Huygens, Taylor, Jonsson, Merli, Tonomura, Arndt, Zeilinger, Rempe). INTRA-SCIENCE LANE: the classical wave-versus-Newton verdict belongs to the optics/light ladder; this one keys the QUANTUM extension — single quanta interfering with themselves.
history_overlap: PHILOSOPHY bank risk (negative guard, not a duplication): philosophy may carry 'observation changes the observed' as an epistemology cliche. Science must not echo it loosely — the T5b rung exists precisely to replace the cliche with the measured mechanism (which-path correlation, not disturbance). No other sister-bank fact is at risk here.

name: Matter is a wave: de Broglie's guess and the bottle that exploded
scope: How a wild thesis got confirmed by an accident nobody wanted. T1: in his 1924 doctoral thesis Louis de Broglie turned Einstein's argument around — if a wave can behave like a particle, why shouldn't a particle behave like a wave? — and wrote down one line, wavelength = h / momentum. His examiners in Paris were unsure enough that Paul Langevin sent the thesis to Einstein, who wrote back that de Broglie had lifted a corner of the great veil. T2 (why you don't diffract through a doorway): h is tiny and your momentum is huge, so a walking person's de Broglie wavelength is about 10^-35 metres — smaller than anything that could ever bend around a door frame. The rule is universal; the effect is only visible when the particle is light and slow. T3 (the accident): in April 1925 a liquid-air bottle exploded next to Clinton Davisson and Lester Germer's apparatus at Bell Labs. Air rushed into the vacuum and oxidized their hot nickel target. To rescue it they baked it in hydrogen for weeks — and the nickel recrystallized from a mass of tiny grains into a few large crystals. When they restarted, the scattered electrons came off in sharp peaks that had never been there before. T4 (what the peaks meant): the angles fitted Bragg's law with exactly the wavelength de Broglie's formula predicted for that electron energy. Davisson shared the 1937 Nobel with George Paget Thomson — whose father, J. J. Thomson, had won the 1906 Nobel for showing the electron is a particle. Father and son, opposite answers, both right. T5 (what it bought us): because a 100 keV electron's wavelength is roughly a hundred thousand times shorter than green light, an electron microscope can resolve individual atoms — the wave nature of matter is the reason we can photograph the things atoms are made of. Deeper rungs: neutron diffraction as the standard tool for locating hydrogen atoms in crystals; the Talbot-Lau interferometer that carries the molecule records; why an electron 'orbit' is really a standing wave that fits a whole number of wavelengths.
source: Grokipedia 'Double-slit experiment' (Davisson-Germer 1927 as the first electron-diffraction confirmation of de Broglie, 1937 Nobel) and Grokipedia 'Davisson-Germer experiment'. Corroborated: Davisson & Germer, 'The Diffraction of Electrons by a Crystal of Nickel', Phys. Rev. 30, 705 (1927); Smithsonian National Museum of American History object record for the Davisson-Germer apparatus; unifyphysics and s4sscienceforstudents accounts of the April 1925 liquid-air-bottle accident, the oxidation and the hydrogen bake that recrystallized the nickel.
framing_note: DISCOVERY ladder built on a serendipity story, which is exactly the bank's 'how we know' voice — the universe handed them the answer through a broken bottle and they were prepared enough to notice. THE ACCURACY RAIL: Davisson and Germer were not looking for matter waves; they were studying electron scattering off metal surfaces, and the recrystallized target is what made the diffraction visible — do not retro-fit them as de Broglie hunters. Second rail: verify the Einstein 'lifted a corner of the great veil' wording before using it as a quote; if it cannot be documented, key the rung to the documented fact that Langevin sent the thesis to Einstein and Einstein's endorsement is what got it taken seriously. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: T3 (an exploding bottle of liquid air is why we know electrons are waves) and T4 (the father proved particle, the son proved wave, both got Nobels). DISTRACTOR MINE: the plum-pudding atom, the planetary Bohr orbit read literally, 'electrons are too small to be waves', X-rays as the true cause of the peaks (a real, checkable alternative they had to exclude), and real adjacent names (Langevin, Bragg, Elsasser, G. P. Thomson, J. J. Thomson, Germer, Schrodinger). INTRA-SCIENCE LANE: single-particle self-interference belongs to the double-slit ladder; this one owns the WAVELENGTH FORMULA and its first accidental confirmation. No rung may be a bare 'what year' or 'what formula symbol' question.

name: Stern, Gerlach, and the cheap cigar
scope: The experiment that made quantization visible as two spots on a plate — and got the right answer for the wrong reason. T1: in Frankfurt in 1922 Otto Stern and Walther Gerlach fired a beam of silver atoms through a deliberately lopsided magnetic field. Classical physics predicts the tiny atomic magnets point every which way, so the beam should arrive as one smeared-out blob. What arrived was TWO separate spots with a clean gap between them — nature refusing every value but two. T2 (the cigar): the silver film was far too thin to see, and Gerlach nearly wrote the run off. The plate darkened only when Stern leaned over it — on a junior salary Stern smoked cheap, sulfur-rich cigars, and his breath converted the invisible silver into jet-black silver sulfide. Bretislav Friedrich and Dudley Herschbach reconstructed the episode in Physics Today in 2003 and confirmed the signal appears only with the bad cigar. T3 (the honest caveat): Stern and Gerlach believed they had confirmed the Bohr-Sommerfeld 'space quantization' of ORBITAL angular momentum. They had not. Electron SPIN was not proposed until 1925 by Samuel Goudsmit and George Uhlenbeck, and silver splits into two because of the spin of its single unpaired outer electron. A landmark result, a wrong explanation, and years before anyone knew. T4 (the sequel a kid can follow): send the 'up' beam into a second magnet turned ninety degrees and it splits again, up and down. Send THAT output back into the first magnet and the up/down split you thought you had fixed comes back. Measuring one direction genuinely erases what you knew about another. T5: that beam-splitting sequence is the uncertainty principle made visible with hardware instead of algebra, and it is why the Stern-Gerlach apparatus is the standard first picture of a quantum measurement.
source: B. Friedrich & D. Herschbach, 'Stern and Gerlach: How a Bad Cigar Helped Reorient Atomic Physics', Physics Today 56(12), 53 (2003), and their 2003 reenactment; B. Friedrich, 'A Century Ago the Stern-Gerlach Experiment Ruled Unequivocally in Favor of Quantum Mechanics', Israel J. Chem. (2023); Quanta Magazine, 'The (Often) Overlooked Experiment That Revealed the Quantum World' (Dec 2023); Nautilus, 'The Overlooked Experiment That Revealed the Quantum World'.
framing_note: DISCOVERY ladder with a corrected-misconception spine and one of the best laboratory anecdotes in physics. THE ACCURACY RAIL: T3 is non-negotiable — do not let any rung say the Stern-Gerlach experiment 'discovered spin' or 'confirmed spin'. It measured a two-way splitting that we now explain by spin; Stern and Gerlach thought they had confirmed Bohr-Sommerfeld orbital space quantization, and spin was proposed three years later by Goudsmit and Uhlenbeck. Second rail: the cigar story is documented and reenacted, but keep it to what Friedrich and Herschbach establish — sulfur in cheap cigar smoke developing silver into silver sulfide — with no embroidery about exact words spoken. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: T2 (a physicist's bad cigars are the reason the plate could be read at all) and T4 (measuring sideways wipes out what you already knew going up). DISTRACTOR MINE: Bohr-Sommerfeld orbital space quantization (the thing they wrongly believed they had shown, and a genuinely live theory at the time), the classical smeared blob, magnetic impurities in the beam, a three-spot pattern (which orbital quantization would have given), and real adjacent names (Sommerfeld, Bohr, Goudsmit, Uhlenbeck, Pauli, Rabi, Ramsey). INTRA-SCIENCE LANE: the FORMAL statement of uncertainty belongs to the uncertainty ladder; here it is a hardware demonstration only, so T5 must key the beams, not the inequality.

name: Heisenberg's uncertainty is not clumsy instruments
scope: A hard limit of nature, dressed for eighty years in the wrong explanation. T1 (checkable at home): pluck a guitar string and hold it, and the note has a definite pitch; pluck it and damp it instantly and there is no pitch at all, just a click. A very short sound simply does not contain a single frequency — a phone tuner will show it. That trade between 'when' and 'what pitch' is the whole idea, and it is true of ocean waves and radio signals with no quantum mechanics anywhere. T2 (Heisenberg's picture, 1927): to see where an electron is you must bounce something off it; short-wavelength light pins the position but hits hard, long-wavelength light is gentle but blurry. He wrote it up as an imaginary gamma-ray microscope and got the trade-off roughly right. T3 (Bohr's objection): Bohr came back from holiday, read the paper and told Heisenberg the microscope argument was misleading — it made the limit sound like a measurement being clumsy, when the real source is that a particle IS a wave packet, and a packet localized in space is built from a spread of wavelengths. Heisenberg added an acknowledging note in proof rather than withdraw the paper. T4 (what the law actually says): Earle Kennard's 1927 inequality, delta-x times delta-p at least h-bar over two, is a statement about PREPARATION, not measurement — no quantum state of any particle, however gently handled, has both a sharp position and a sharp momentum. Howard Robertson generalized it to any pair of incompatible quantities in 1929. T5 (the modern separation): in 2012 two teams — Erhart and colleagues in Vienna using neutron spins, and Rozema and colleagues in Toronto using photon polarization with weak measurements — VIOLATED Heisenberg's naive error-times-disturbance product while Kennard's relation stood completely untouched, exactly as Masanao Ozawa's corrected 2003 relation predicted. Two different statements had been wearing one name, and only one of them was ever a law. Deeper rungs: zero-point motion — helium will not freeze at ordinary pressure no matter how cold you make it, because an atom is forbidden to sit still at the bottom of a well; the energy-time version and why unstable particles have fuzzy masses; why an atom's electron does not spiral into the nucleus.
source: Grokipedia 'Uncertainty principle' (Heisenberg 1927 and the microscope thought experiment, Kennard's 1927 inequality, Robertson 1929, the Fourier-transform foundation and the wave-packet motivation, Ozawa's 2003 universally valid error-disturbance relation, and the neutron-spin and photon-polarization experiments that violate the naive relation while satisfying Ozawa's). Corroborated on the Fourier/signal-processing framing and the preparation-versus-measurement distinction within the same article's 'Error-Disturbance Tradeoff' section.
framing_note: MECHANISM + corrected-misconception ladder, and the single most-misused idea in popular science — the bank's job is to hand the kid the correct version. THE ACCURACY RAIL: no rung may present the uncertainty principle as the observer effect or as a limit of instrument quality. T4 is the load-bearing rung: it is a fact about what states EXIST, not about how carefully you look. Second rail: verify the detail of Bohr's return and the note added in proof before authoring T3; if the personal scene cannot be documented, key the rung to Bohr's SUBSTANTIVE objection (wave packet, not disturbance), which is well established. Do not use the 'Heisenberg was reduced to tears' anecdote unless a primary source is found. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: T1 (a very short note has no pitch — go make one) and T5 (an experiment beat the version of the principle everybody quotes, and the real one never moved). DISTRACTOR MINE: the observer effect, 'better instruments will fix it', the idea that the particle secretly has both values and we just cannot see them (this is the hidden-variable option that the Bell ladder kills, so keep the two ladders consistent), and real adjacent names (Bohr, Kennard, Robertson, Schrodinger, Ozawa, Born, Jordan, Pauli). TEACH BEFORE TESTING: introduce 'wave packet' and 'standard deviation as spread' in an earlier rung than any rung that leans on them. INTRA-SCIENCE LANE: the hardware demonstration of incompatible measurements belongs to the Stern-Gerlach ladder; this one owns the statement and its history.
history_overlap: PHILOSOPHY bank risk: philosophy may carry determinism, free will, and 'the limits of what can be known' as seminar topics, and the uncertainty principle is routinely dragged into all three. Science owns only the physical statement and the experiments; no rung here may argue about free will or about whether reality is deterministic. If a philosophy ladder already uses uncertainty as an epistemology example, this ladder is the factual corrective and must not restate the seminar move.

name: Schrodinger's cat was a rebuke
scope: The most famous thought experiment in physics, almost universally quoted backwards. T1 (the box): a cat, a Geiger counter, a speck of radioactive material with about a fifty-fifty chance of a single decay in one hour, a relay, a hammer, and a flask of hydrocyanic acid. If the atom decays the counter fires, the hammer falls, the flask breaks and the cat dies. T2 (THE CORRECTION): Erwin Schrodinger was not celebrating the idea of a cat both alive and dead. He built the box to make that idea look ridiculous — a reduction to absurdity aimed straight at the Copenhagen view, in 'Die gegenwartige Situation in der Quantenmechanik', Naturwissenschaften 23, 807 (1935), where he calls it a burlesque case. The cat is an accusation, not a doctrine. T3 (whose side he was on): Einstein had written to him that year about a keg of gunpowder which quantum mechanics would describe as a smear of exploded and unexploded; the cat is Schrodinger's sharpened version of Einstein's complaint, and the two men egged each other on by letter through 1935. T4 (the irony): in that same 1935 paper Schrodinger coined the word Verschrankung — entanglement — and called it 'not one but rather THE characteristic trait of quantum mechanics, the one that enforces its entire departure from classical lines of thought.' His attack on the theory named its crown jewel; entanglement is now the working substance of quantum cryptography and quantum computing. T5 (what we know now that he did not): decoherence. A real cat exchanges photons and air molecules with its surroundings constantly; the superposition leaks away into the environment in far less than a nanosecond, long before anyone opens the lid, so the cat is never in any state a laboratory could distinguish from ordinary alive-or-dead. Serge Haroche's Paris group actually WATCHED a small 'cat state' of a few microwave photons in a mirrored cavity decohere step by step, and confirmed the rule that the bigger the cat, the faster it dies — work recognized with the 2012 Nobel shared with David Wineland. Deeper rungs: the paper drew only about 26 citations in its first forty years; how the phrase escaped into pop culture; why 'the cat is dead AND alive' is a worse summary than 'the theory, taken literally, says something absurd here.'
source: Grokipedia "Schrodinger's cat" (1935 Naturwissenschaften 23, 807-812; explicit reductio ad absurdum against the Copenhagen interpretation; the sealed chamber with radioactive substance, Geiger counter and hydrocyanic acid at fifty percent in one hour; Einstein's August 1935 letters; only ~26 citations in the first forty years; the entanglement of apparatus with the cat). Corroborated: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Quantum Entanglement and Information', for Schrodinger's 1935 'not one but rather the characteristic trait of quantum mechanics' wording.
framing_note: The bank's flagship CORRECTED-MISCONCEPTION rung in this sub-strand — the whole ladder exists because the popular version inverts the author's meaning. THE ACCURACY RAIL: never write a stem or an answer that treats the cat as evidence FOR superposition of large objects. Schrodinger's target was the Copenhagen interpretation, and the German word to verify before quoting is 'burlesk' in the phrase describing the case; quote the German only if the primary text is checked, otherwise say 'he called the case ridiculous' and cite the paper. Second rail: decoherence explains why we never SEE the superposition; it does not by itself say why one outcome happens — do not let T5 overclaim, and hand the leftover to the measurement-mystery ladder. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: the stem describing the box must never contain the word 'rebuke', 'criticize' or 'absurd' before asking what Schrodinger meant by it — describe the apparatus and let the intent be recalled knowledge. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: T2 (everybody quotes it backwards) and T4 (the man attacking the theory named its best idea). DISTRACTOR MINE: 'he was showing off how strange quantum mechanics is', 'he was defending the Copenhagen interpretation', 'consciousness collapses the wave function' (the von Neumann-Wigner view, genuinely held by serious physicists and now out of favour), and real adjacent names (Bohr, Heisenberg, Einstein, Podolsky, Rosen, von Neumann, Wigner, Everett, Haroche, Zurek).
history_overlap: PHILOSOPHY bank risk: philosophy owns 'reductio ad absurdum' as a REASONING MOVE and may already teach it with a named example; science owns Schrodinger's actual 1935 paper and what it argued. No rung here may ask the player to identify or name the argument form — that is the philosophy bank's job. Keep every answer here a concrete physical or historical fact (the apparatus, the target, the coined word, the decoherence result).

name: From Einstein's spooky action to the 2022 Nobel: a philosophical fight settled by experiment
scope: The keystone THEME ladder — how an argument two of the greatest physicists could not win with words became a measurement anyone could run. T1 (the objection): make two particles together, carry one to Paris and one to Tokyo, and measuring the first instantly fixes what the second will say. Einstein could not accept it, and in a letter to Max Born on 3 March 1947 he called it 'spukhafte Fernwirkung' — spooky action at a distance. T2 (the argument, 1935): in Physical Review on 15 May 1935 Einstein, Boris Podolsky and Nathan Rosen argued that if you can predict the distant particle's value with certainty without touching it, that value must have been REAL all along — so quantum mechanics is incomplete and the particles must be carrying hidden instructions, like twins leaving home with sealed envelopes. T3 (the turn): for twenty-nine years this looked like a matter of taste. Then John Stewart Bell, a CERN accelerator physicist doing foundations as a hobby, published 'On the Einstein Podolsky Rosen Paradox' in 1964 and showed the two pictures make DIFFERENT numerical predictions when the two detectors are set to different angles: any sealed-envelope theory must obey an inequality, and quantum mechanics predicts breaking it. Taste became arithmetic. T4 (the first test): in 1972 at Berkeley, Stuart Freedman and John Clauser used a calcium atomic cascade to emit entangled photon pairs, set polarizers 1.35 metres apart at 22.5 and 67.5 degrees, and watched the inequality break. T5a (closing the escapes): Alain Aspect's Orsay team in 1981-82 used acousto-optic switches to change the analyzer settings every 10 nanoseconds — after the photons had already left the source — over a 12-metre baseline, measuring S = 2.25 plus or minus 0.02 against a local-realist ceiling of 2. In 2015 three groups (Hanson in Delft, Shalm at NIST, Giustina in Vienna) closed the detection and locality loopholes at once. In 2018 a Vienna-led team set the detectors using the colours of photons from two quasars whose light left 7.8 and 12.2 billion years ago, and the BIG Bell Test used random bits typed by more than a hundred thousand human volunteers. T5b (the human cost and the vindication): Clauser's senior colleagues at Columbia warned him that testing quantum mechanics would destroy his career; Feynman told him he was offended by his impertinence; when the results came in, they told him it was a waste of time and to go do some real physics. In 2022 Clauser, Aspect and Zeilinger shared the Nobel Prize. T5c (the hard limit, stated honestly): entanglement cannot send a message. Each side's results alone look like pure coin-flip noise; the correlation only appears when the two lists of outcomes are brought together, and that has to travel at light speed or slower. Deeper rungs: the Tsirelson bound of 2 times root 2 as the ceiling nature actually uses; superdeterminism as the one surviving escape and why Bell called it a conspiracy; Bell violation as a WORKING TOOL today (device-independent key distribution, certified randomness).

Corroborated: Rauch et al., 'Cosmic Bell Test Using Random Measurement Settings from High-Redshift Quasars', Phys. Rev. Lett. 121, 080403 (2018) and IQOQI Vienna's Cosmic Bell Experiments page; the BIG Bell Test (2018); NobelPrize.org 2022 Clauser interview transcript, AIP oral history 'Entanglement and experiment, part 2', and the PNAS profile of the 2022 laureates for the career warnings and Feynman's reaction; en.wiktionary.org and the Born-Einstein Letters for the 3 March 1947 'spukhafte Fernwirkung' letter.
framing_note: THE analytic backbone of the sub-strand and the bank's clearest case of mode-2 REVERSAL plus mode-4 MECHANISM: a question everyone called metaphysics turned out to have a number attached. THE ACCURACY RAIL (most important in this ladder): T5c is mandatory and no earlier rung may contradict it — entanglement transmits NO information and nothing travels faster than light; the correlation is only visible after the two data sets meet. Never write 'measuring here changes the particle there' as a bare claim. Second rail: Bell's theorem rules out LOCAL hidden variables, not all hidden variables — Bohm's pilot-wave theory is explicitly nonlocal and survives; say it that precisely. Third rail: verify the exact Clauser quotes ('waste of time... now start doing some real physics'; Feynman's offence) against the NobelPrize.org interview transcript or the AIP oral history before authoring T5b, and attribute them to the source. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: T3 (a hobby paper turned a philosophical stalemate into an experiment) and T5a (the settings were chosen by light from quasars older than the Earth). DISTRACTOR MINE: local hidden variables and the sealed-envelope picture (the real, respectable, now-dead theory — the richest mine here), the detection loophole, the locality loophole, the freedom-of-choice loophole, superdeterminism, and real adjacent names (Podolsky, Rosen, Born, Bohm, Shimony, Horne, Holt, Freedman, Hanson, Giustina, Shalm, Zeilinger). Never let a distractor be a live rival that is secretly true.
history_overlap: PHILOSOPHY bank risk: realism versus anti-realism, and the demarcation question of what counts as a scientific rather than a metaphysical claim, are philosophy-bank seminar moves. This ladder must stay on the EXPERIMENTS and the people — what was measured, where, with what settings, and what it excluded — and must not ask the player to adjudicate realism. Flagged vision_mandated=true for one reason only: the documented institutional discouragement of foundations research (Clauser warned it would end his career, Feynman's dismissal, 'shut up and calculate' as the era's mood) is a real dissent-and-vindication thread the bank's stance says to tell honestly. Tell it as documented fact with named sources, never as a lesson or a grievance; the physics rungs carry the ladder and the stance rung is one rung of thirteen. Accuracy sub-rail for that rung: 'shut up and calculate' was coined by N. David Mermin in a 1989 Physics Today column and is routinely misattributed to Feynman — Mermin himself wrote the correction; if the phrase is used, the misattribution IS the wonder.

name: Quantum tunnelling: why the Sun shines and your flash drive remembers
scope: The particle that goes through the wall, from stellar cores to the memory stick in a drawer. T1 (the impossible sum): the Sun's core is about fifteen million degrees, which sounds enormous, but two protons need roughly 500 keV of energy to shove past their mutual electric repulsion and the typical particle there carries only about 1.3 keV — a factor of hundreds short. The protons do not climb the barrier. They go THROUGH it. T2 (what tunnelling is): a quantum particle is described by a wave, and a wave does not stop dead at a barrier — it decays inside it. If the barrier is thin enough, a little of the wave comes out the far side, which means a real, calculable probability of finding the particle there. The probability falls off exponentially with thickness, which is why it is invisible for cricket balls and decisive for protons. T3 (the first payoff): in 1928 the 24-year-old George Gamow and, independently, Ronald Gurney and Edward Condon, used tunnelling to explain alpha decay — an alpha particle inside a uranium nucleus is trapped behind a barrier taller than its own energy, yet uranium decays. Tunnelling reproduced the Geiger-Nuttall law, which stretches across roughly twenty-four orders of magnitude in half-life over a narrow range of alpha energies. T4 (the man who was right for the wrong reason): eight years before Gamow, Arthur Eddington had already insisted the stars run on hydrogen fusion. Told the stars were not hot enough, he replied in 1920 that he would not argue with such a critic — 'we tell him to go and find a hotter place.' He had no idea why he was right; tunnelling supplied the reason after the fact. T5a (why the Sun burns slowly): even with tunnelling, the very first step of the proton-proton chain also requires the weak force to turn one proton into a neutron, and that is so improbable that a given proton in the solar core waits on the order of billions of years for it. The Sun is a spectacularly BAD reactor, which is exactly why it has lasted long enough for us. T5b (tunnelling you can buy): Gerd Binnig and Heinrich Rohrer's scanning tunnelling microscope (IBM Zurich, 1981; Nobel 1986) holds a needle a few atoms above a surface and measures the tunnelling current, which changes by roughly a factor of ten for every 0.1 nanometre of height — sensitive enough to map single atoms; in 1989 Don Eigler used one to spell 'IBM' in 35 xenon atoms. Your USB stick stores every bit by driving electrons THROUGH an insulator onto a floating gate, and the same effect leaks charge out of the tiniest transistors, which is a design headache rather than a bonus. Deeper rungs: Friedrich Hund's 1927 ammonia inversion — the nitrogen atom tunnels through the plane of three hydrogens billions of times a second, and that oscillation ran the first atomic clock in 1949; Leo Esaki's 1957 tunnel diode and the 1973 Nobel shared with Ivar Giaever and Brian Josephson; the 2025 Nobel to John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis for showing that a whole superconducting CIRCUIT, not just a particle, can tunnel.
source: Grokipedia 'Quantum tunnelling' (Hund 1927 ammonia inversion as the first application; Gamow 1928 and independently Gurney and Condon 1928 for alpha decay and the Geiger-Nuttall law; the proton-proton chain tunnelling through a ~500 keV barrier at ~15 million K; Esaki's 1957 tunnel diode and the 1973 Nobel with Giaever and Josephson; Binnig and Rohrer's 1981 STM and the 1986 Nobel; gate leakage and flash memory; the 2025 Nobel to Clarke, Devoret and Martinis for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in an electrical circuit, based on 1984-85 Josephson-junction experiments). Corroborated: Physics World, 'Explorer of stars and souls: Arthur Stanley Eddington', and en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Arthur_Eddington for the 1920 'go and find a hotter place' retort (The Observatory, October 1920, repeated in The Internal Constitution of the Stars, 1926).
framing_note: MECHANISM ladder with the widest reach in the sub-strand — it connects a star to a flash drive without a single equation. THE ACCURACY RAIL: verify the proton-waiting-time figure for the first step of the pp chain before authoring T5a and state it as an order of magnitude ('billions of years' rather than a false-precision number); the qualitative point — the weak-interaction first step, not tunnelling, is the real bottleneck — is what the rung must carry. Second rail: the 2025 Nobel is very recent; confirm the laureates and citation wording against NobelPrize.org before authoring that rung, and drop it rather than guess. Third rail: quote Eddington's retort exactly and date it to his 1920 remarks, noting he made the claim BEFORE tunnelling existed as an idea — that ordering is the whole wonder of T4 and must not be blurred. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: T1 (the Sun is a thousand times too cold to work, and works anyway) and T5b (the pictures of individual atoms you have seen were taken by measuring particles going through a wall). DISTRACTOR MINE: the classical 'the core must be hotter than we think' answer that Eddington's critics actually gave, the ether, 'the alpha particle is knocked out by a collision', 'the barrier gets lower at high pressure', and real adjacent names (Gamow, Gurney, Condon, Hund, Eddington, Bethe, Geiger, Nuttall, Esaki, Giaever, Josephson, Binnig, Rohrer). INTRA-SCIENCE LANE: the science bank's astronomy strand owns the Sun's life cycle, Cecilia Payne's hydrogen composition and Bethe's CNO cycle — this ladder must key ONLY the barrier-penetration mechanism and its technology, not re-tour stellar structure.
history_overlap: GEOGRAPHY bank risk: geography's earth-system strand already tours the Sun as the driver of insolation, seasons and climate. This ladder must never spend a rung on what sunlight DOES to Earth — it stays inside the nuclear mechanism and its laboratory descendants. No sister-bank fact is otherwise at risk; the Manhattan Project and wartime nuclear physics belong to the history bank and appear nowhere here.

name: The quantum tech already in your pocket
scope: The strangest theory in physics is also the most profitable, and the kid is holding several billion pieces of the evidence. T1 (invert the wonder): writing in Scientific American in February 2001, Max Tegmark and John Wheeler put it at an estimated thirty percent of United States gross national product resting on inventions that quantum mechanics made possible — and named the two families that carry most of it, semiconductors and lasers. T2 (the moment): on 16 December 1947 John Bardeen and Walter Brattain pressed two gold contacts a hair's width apart onto a slab of high-purity germanium and got an output signal about a hundred times bigger than the input; on 23 December they demonstrated it to Bell Labs management by switching it in and out of an audio circuit so everyone could hear the amplification. William Shockley's more manufacturable junction transistor followed within weeks, and the three shared the 1956 Nobel. T3 (why it is quantum, not just clever): in an isolated atom electrons may only occupy certain energies; pack atoms into a crystal and those levels smear into BANDS with forbidden gaps between them. Whether a material conducts, insulates, or can be switched between the two depends entirely on that gap — a purely quantum result with no classical version, and the reason silicon can be persuaded to behave like both. T4 (the band gap you can see): an LED is that gap made visible — an electron falls across it and emits exactly one photon whose colour the gap energy fixes. Nick Holonyak built the first visible (red) LED at General Electric in 1962. Red and green were straightforward; BLUE took three decades and gallium nitride, and Isamu Akasaki, Hiroshi Amano and Shuji Nakamura took the 2014 Nobel 'for the invention of efficient blue light-emitting diodes which has enabled bright and energy-saving white light sources' — every white LED bulb in the house is a blue LED wearing a yellow coat. T5a (the laser nobody wanted): Theodore Maiman fired the first working laser at Hughes Research Laboratories on 16 May 1960, using ruby — a material other groups had written off. T5b (test it yourself): shine a cheap laser pointer at the surface of a CD or DVD and the microscopic track spacing acts as a diffraction grating, throwing a row of spots on the wall whose angles let you measure the wavelength of your own laser on the kitchen table. T5c (the honest caveat): transistors, lasers and LEDs are settled, everywhere, and quantum through and through. A general-purpose quantum COMPUTER that beats an ordinary computer on a problem someone actually wants solved does not yet exist — error correction is the open obstacle — and the bank should say so rather than blur the two.
source: M. Tegmark & J. A. Wheeler, '100 Years of Quantum Mysteries', Scientific American 284(2), 68-75 (February 2001), for the estimated thirty-percent-of-GNP sentence; Computer History Museum, '1947: Invention of the Point-Contact Transistor', and ETHW 'Bell Demonstrates Transistor' / 'Milestones: Invention of the First Transistor at Bell Telephone Laboratories, 1947' for the 16 and 23 December 1947 dates and the ~100x amplification; NobelPrize.org, Physics 1956 (Shockley, Bardeen, Brattain); SPIE, 'The light fantastic: Ted Maiman and the world's first laser' and HRL Laboratories 'The Laser' for 16 May 1960; GE News and IEEE Photonics Society on Nick Holonyak's 1962 first visible LED; NobelPrize.org 2014 press release (Akasaki, Amano, Nakamura) for the blue-LED citation wording; Grokipedia 'Quantum tunnelling' for gate leakage and flash-memory tunnelling as the same physics.
framing_note: MECHANISM ladder that pays off the whole sub-strand: everything strange in the other nine ladders is load-bearing in the kid's own house. THE ACCURACY RAIL: the thirty-percent figure is an ESTIMATE by two named authors in a named article, not a measured statistic — the stem must attribute it ('Tegmark and Wheeler estimated...') and the ANSWER must be the technology family, never the number. Second rail: verify before use the widely repeated claim that Maiman's laser paper was rejected by Physical Review Letters and published in Nature instead, and likewise the 'a solution looking for a problem' quip attributed to his assistant Irnee D'Haenens — if either cannot be documented to a primary source, drop the rung rather than soften it; there is enough verified material without them. Third rail: T5c is mandatory and must not be quietly dropped for a tidier ending — the bank does not let a settled-technology ladder imply that quantum computing is already delivering. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: T4 (every white bulb in the house is a blue LED with a yellow phosphor on it) and T5b (measure your own laser's wavelength with a CD). DISTRACTOR MINE: vacuum tubes and the relay as the real predecessors the transistor displaced, 'it is just a very small switch, no quantum mechanics needed', the incandescent filament, and real adjacent names (Shockley, Bardeen, Brattain, Kilby, Noyce, Townes, Schawlow, Maiman, Holonyak, Nakamura, Esaki). TEACH BEFORE TESTING: define 'band gap' in T3 before any rung leans on it in T4. INTRA-SCIENCE LANE: tunnelling-specific devices (STM, flash memory) belong to the tunnelling ladder; this one owns band structure, amplification and light emission.
history_overlap: HISTORY bank risk: the transistor and Bell Labs as a postwar American economic and industrial story, and Silicon Valley's founding, are history-bank material. This ladder must key the PHYSICS — the band gap, the amplification, the photon emitted across the gap — and never turn a rung into a corporate or economic-history question. Also avoid any rung that is a bare Nobel-year or company-name recall item.

name: The measurement problem: the part no one has solved
scope: A short MYSTERY ladder that refuses to pretend. T4 (what Bell settled and what it did not): the experiments killed LOCAL hidden variables for good. They did not choose between the surviving pictures. Copenhagen, Hugh Everett's 1957 many-worlds, and the explicitly nonlocal pilot-wave theory of de Broglie and David Bohm all reproduce every result any laboratory has ever obtained — no experiment has yet distinguished them, and honest physicists disagree about which is right. T5a (what decoherence did and did not fix): Dieter Zeh and Wojciech Zurek showed why we never SEE a large object in superposition — the system leaks its phase relations into its environment almost instantly, so interference between the alternatives becomes unobservable. That explains the absence of visible weirdness. It does not, by itself, explain why exactly ONE outcome happens rather than the others, and saying otherwise is overclaiming. T5b (the part that IS being tested): objective-collapse theories such as Ghirardi-Rimini-Weber (1986) and the Diosi-Penrose gravity-driven proposal are not interpretations — they predict a real, mass-dependent breakdown of superposition, which means they can be RULED OUT. Every new record in molecule interference and every underground low-background search squeezes their allowed parameter range further, and some versions are already excluded. A question that sounded like pure metaphysics turned into an experimental programme with a budget.
source: Grokipedia "Schrodinger's cat" (Everett's 1957 many-worlds; decoherence and environmental entanglement as the account of why macroscopic superpositions are not observed) and Grokipedia "Bell's theorem" (what the experiments exclude: local hidden variables, with nonlocal hidden-variable theories surviving). Corroborated: Fein et al., Nature Physics 15, 1242 (2019), which states explicitly that increasing interfering mass places more stringent bounds on modified quantum theories such as objective collapse models; Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Quantum Entanglement and Information'.
framing_note: Mode-3 MYSTERY ladder — the bank says 'no one yet knows' with a straight face, and shows that the honest version is more interesting than a fake resolution. THE ACCURACY RAIL, and it governs every rung: no distractor may secretly be the truth, and no rung may crown a winner. Many-worlds, Copenhagen and pilot-wave are LIVE and must all appear as live; the correct answer on T4 is that no experiment has separated them. Corollary: never write 'scientists now believe many-worlds' or 'the wave function really collapses' as a settled fact. Second rail: keep the tone confident, not hand-wringing — the T5b rung is the point of the ladder, because it shows that a piece of the mystery was successfully dragged into the lab and is being narrowed by real measurements. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: T5b (a metaphysical-sounding question with an experiment attached and a shrinking answer space). DISTRACTOR MINE: 'consciousness collapses the wave function' (the von Neumann-Wigner position, once held by serious physicists, now marginal), 'decoherence solved it', 'Bell ruled out all hidden variables' (the precise, common error this ladder corrects), and real adjacent names (Everett, Bohm, Zeh, Zurek, Ghirardi, Rimini, Weber, Penrose, Diosi, Wigner, DeWitt). TEACH BEFORE TESTING: 'decoherence' and 'hidden variable' must both be defined in earlier rungs of the Bell and cat ladders before this mini leans on them — this ladder assumes those two are already shipped.
history_overlap: PHILOSOPHY bank risk, and it is the largest in the sub-strand: interpretations of quantum mechanics shade directly into realism, idealism and the limits of scientific knowledge, which are philosophy-bank territory. The border is strict here — every rung must be answerable by naming a THEORY, an EXPERIMENT or a MEASURED BOUND, never by taking a metaphysical position. If the philosophy bank already carries a 'what is real' ladder that mentions quantum mechanics, this mini is the factual companion and must not restate its seminar move.
